title: Automated Pin Assistant + Version Archival Procedure
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We need a repeatable, low-friction way to retire older model versions while minimizing customer disruption and ensuring customers can pin to compatible replacements. This ticket defines an automated 'Pin Assistant' plus an archival workflow that ties together: notice cadence, SDK/console warnings, published performance/compatibility profiles, migration guides, and telemetry-driven thresholds for archival.

Scope: - Automate identification of candidate versions for archival based on age, usage decline, performance regression signals, and maintenance cost. - Surface recommended replacement(s) with: compatibility matrix (API/response shape), token-cost delta, latency and throughput profile, quantization/precision differences, and example migration diffs. - Implement staged communication: pre-warning (60d), mandatory pin-warning (30d), imminent-archival (7d), archival (0d). - Ensure customers with active pins or Dedicated/Private contracts get tailored timelines and support. - Publish migration artifacts (guides, PR templates, SDK warning copy) and console flags.

Trade-offs considered: - Aggressive archival shortens model sprawl but raises customer effort. We bias toward longer grace periods for pinned customers and a programmatic auto-pin suggestion rather than forced migration. - Automation complexity vs manual coordination: fully automated archival requires strong telemetry and robust rollback; initial rollout will be semi-automated with PM/OSS review gates.

Stakeholders: - Product (Ava Chen, owner) - Runtime/Serving (Lina Patel) - SDK/Developer Experience (Omar Hassan) - Console/UX (Priya Nair) - Customer Success & Sales (Evan Brooks) - Legal/Compliance (Nia Fernandez)

Acceptance criteria (high level): - Pin Assistant prototype surfaces at least 2 compatible replacement recommendations per candidate version with performance and cost delta. - Automated email/console notification pipeline for the 60d/30d/7d stages is operational for hosted customers. - SDK injects deprecation warning for pinned but deprecated versions and provides migration snippet. - A rollback path is documented; archival can be reverted within 72 hours by engineers with audit trail. - Telemetry dashboards show adoption metrics and migration completion rates.
acceptance_criteria: Pin Assistant lists >=2 replacement candidates with compatibility notes and cost/latency deltas
Notifications (60d/30d/7d) show up in Console and email for affected active API keys
SDKs (python/js) emit non-fatal warnings when clients request deprecated versions; warnings include link to migration guide
Migration guide templates published in Confluence and linked from Console
Archival action appears as an auditable change in customer activity log with rollback support (<=72h)
Dashboards track: affected customers, pinned installs, migration completions, and failure/rollback incidents
tasks: Define archival candidate scoring heuristic (age, monthly qps, error rate, maintenance cost)
Design Console UX: deprecation badge, timeline banner, and 'Accept Replacement' CTA
Implement Pin Assistant service that queries model catalog and computes compatibility scores
Publish per-version performance and compatibility profiles (docs + JSON) to model-catalog endpoint
Add SDK warning hooks and migration-snippet generator in python/js SDKs
Build notification pipeline: staged emails, in-console banners, and account-level tickets for enterprise customers
Create migration guide templates and one worked example for an in-house model pair
Run a canary: pick 3 low-impact legacy versions and run full workflow end-to-end
Instrument dashboards: adoption, conversion rate, rollback frequency, customer outreach workload
Document runbook for emergency rollback and SLA exceptions for Dedicated/Private customers
